title: Open quantum system approach to the Unruh-DeWitt detector in impulsive plane wave spacetimes
abstract: In this paper we employ the open quantum system framework with the influence functional formalism to non-perturbatively analyze the response of an Unruh-DeWitt detector modeled as a harmonic oscillator which interacts with a massless scalar field in impulsive plane wave spacetimes. Subtracting the Minkowski results, we obtain the expectation values for $\langle Q^2 \rangle$, $\langle P^2 \rangle$, and $\langle \{Q,P\} \rangle$, along with transition probabilities $P_{0\rightarrow 1}$ from ground state to the first excited state of the detector due to the influence of the wave. Explicit calculations are performed for both a pure gravitational wave (vanishing Ricci tensor) and a null electromagnetic wave (vanishing Weyl tensor). In both scenarios, the wave suppresses excitation transitions. Since our approach is non-perturbative, we are able to consider cases with both weak and strong coupling constants.
summary: This paper investigates how an Unruh-DeWitt detector responds to impulsive plane waves in curved spacetime using the open quantum system formalism. By calculating expectation values and transition probabilities non-perturbatively, the authors demonstrate that the wave field generally suppresses detector excitations. The results allow for a direct comparison between the effects induced by gravitational versus electromagnetic waves.
main_problem: The paper non-perturbatively analyzes the quantum response of an Unruh-DeWitt detector to the highly non-trivial background of impulsive plane wave spacetimes.
main_result: The presence of the impulsive wave generally suppresses excitation transitions ($P_{0	o 1}$) compared to the initial state, and the electromagnetic wave exerts a stronger effect than the gravitational wave for similar parameters.
method: The analysis employs the open quantum system framework using the influence functional formalism within the closed-time-path path integral approach.
model_or_system: The system consists of an Unruh-DeWitt detector modeled as a harmonic oscillator interacting with a massless scalar field in a curved spacetime background characterized by impulsive plane waves (either pure gravitational or null electromagnetic).
key_observables: Expectation values $\langle Q^2 angle$, $\langle P^2 angle$, $\langle \{Q, P\} angle$, and the transition probability $P_{0	o 1}$ from the ground state to the first excited state.
important_parameters: Wave strength ($\eta_1, \eta_2$), dissipation coefficient ($\gamma$), and the coupling constant (analyzed non-perturbatively).
main_assumptions: The initial state is assumed to be uncorrelated between the detector and the field, and the method relies on the field action being at most quadratic in the path integral evaluation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of expectation values ($\Delta\langle Q^2angle$, $\Delta\langle P^2angle$, $\Delta\langle\{Q, P\}angle$) and transition probabilities ($\Delta P_{0	o 1}$) for both gravitational and electromagnetic waves, showing parameter dependence.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework using the influence functional formalism, derives the evolution operator and reduced density matrix, calculates the expectation values and transition probabilities for impulsive waves, and finally compares the results for gravitational versus electromagnetic backgrounds.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it applies advanced open quantum system techniques (influence functional) to fundamental problems in quantum field theory in curved spacetime, bridging quantum optics/dissipation with general relativity.
